mechanisms.name: spill-store-service-seam
mechanisms.what: Abstract Service Definition for the `ctx.spillStore` capability. `abstract class SpillStore extends Service` registers the service key `spillStore` in its constructor (super(ctx, 'spillStore')) and declares exactly one abstract member, `saveText(input: SaveTextSpill): Promise<SpillRef>`. The module doc states the seam owns NO retention policy, NO tool-result replacement and NO retrieval/search API; the backend supplies the locator and the retrieval hint. `SpillLocator` is a Branded<'SpillLocator'> string; `SpillRef` carries { locator, bytes, retrievalHint }. Production callers of the service are spill-policy, tool-fs-search and session-reference (all via ctx.get('spillStore')).
invariants: saveText persists the FULL content verbatim and returns an opaque locator, exact byte length, and model-facing retrieval guidance (packages/spill/spill/src/index.ts:36-37).

Storage is scoped by the request's SaveTextSpill.owner session; the backend chooses a private (not world-readable) location and a collision-free name derived from — never equal to — the caller's suggestedName (packages/spill/spill/src/index.ts:38-40).
saveText REJECTS on a real storage failure (permissions, ENOSPC, backend unavailable); the caller decides how to degrade (packages/spill/spill/src/index.ts:41-43).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed (the seam contract requires rejection on real storage failure; the decision of how to degrade is pushed to the caller)
constants: no numeric thresholds in this package

mechanisms.name: local-spill-store-session-scoped-private-write
mechanisms.what: `LocalSpillStore extends SpillStore` (packages/spill/spill-local/src/index.ts:65) implements `saveText` by delegating to `saveTextFile` from ./store.ts and returning a path locator plus a fixed retrieval hint string. Path selection is traversal-safe: `sessionDir()` joins `<root>` with `session-<sha256(sessionId) hex sliced to 12 chars>`, `encodeSegment()` injectively escapes every non-`[A-Za-z0-9._-]` code unit as `~XXXX`, and the filename is `<6 random bytes as hex>-<encoded suggestedName>`. The write itself is `mkdir(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` then `open(path, 'wx', 0o600)` in a retry loop that only retries on ENOENT; the file content is written through the returned handle and the byte count is `Buffer.byteLength(content,'utf8')`. Config `root` is optional (lazily created 0700 per-process `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'dsh-spill-'))`).
invariants: A session id / suggested name is untrusted input, so encodeSegment neutralizes `../`, absolute paths, NUL, and separators before any filesystem use; the whole-segment tokens `.`/`..` are escaped so they can never traverse (packages/spill/spill-local/src/store.ts:46-51).
a spilled tool result must not be readable by other local users or redirectable via a planted symlink (packages/spill/spill-local/src/index.ts:56-58).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed (saveTextFile throws; LocalSpillStore.saveText propagates the rejection to the caller per the seam contract)
constants: random name prefix: randomBytes(6) → 12 hex chars — packages/spill/spill-local/src/store.ts:110
retrievalHint literal: 'Use read with offset/limit, or grep this path to search within it.' — packages/spill/spill-local/src/index.ts:159

mechanisms.name: spill-startup-cleanup-sweep
mechanisms.what: After activation, `LocalSpillStore` launches exactly ONE best-effort sweep via `ctx.effect(function* ...)` that starts `runCleanup(warn)` without awaiting it, and yields an async disposer that awaits that same promise; when `cleanupPeriodDays === 0` the disposer is a no-op. `runCleanup` computes `cutoffMs = Date.now() - cleanupPeriodDays * MS_PER_DAY`, gathers roots through `gatherSweepRoots(activeRoot, warn, defaultRootsBase())`, and calls `sweepSpillRoots`. The sweep deletes only regular files whose `mtimeMs` is strictly older than the cutoff (files exactly at the boundary are kept), prunes emptied session directories, and prunes a DISCOVERED prior-default root only when nothing remains; the active root is never pruned. Root discovery matches the exact `mkdtemp` shape `^dsh-spill-[A-Za-z0-9]{6}$` and session directories match `^session-[0-9a-f]{12}$`. On POSIX each root and every ancestor must be current-user-owned with `(mode & 0o022) === 0` (a writable-but-sticky ancestor is accepted), and symlinks are never followed. It has a production caller: the `spill-local` entry in the base profile (packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:380-381).
invariants: Every filesystem and warning-sink failure is contained, so a caller can await this during activation/disposal without it ever rejecting (packages/spill/spill-local/src/cleanup.ts:267-269).
Only regular files expire. Symlinks and other special entries are skipped (never followed) so the sweep cannot be redirected or delete a link (packages/spill/spill-local/src/cleanup.ts:253-255).
Retention is deliberate — a resumed or forked session may still reference an older locator until it ages out (packages/spill/spill-local/src/index.ts:44-46).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft (sweepSpillRoots contains every error and reports it through a warn sink that is itself wrapped by warnSafely; it never rejects and cannot fail activation or a concurrent spill write)
constants: cleanupPeriodDays default 30; 0 disables cleanup — packages/spill/spill-local/src/index.ts:68 (schema default) and 96 (disable gate)
cutoff comparison is strict: `if (stats.mtimeMs >= cutoffMs) continue` (only strictly-older expires) — packages/spill/spill-local/src/cleanup.ts:256

mechanisms.name: output-spill-to-file-with-preview-locator
mechanisms.what:
Cordis plugin `spill-policy` (name = 'spill-policy', inject = ['tools']) that prepends a `tools/post-execute` waterfall listener. The listener first awaits `next()` so downstream listeners settle the result; it then applies, in order: decision must be `kind === 'accept'`, `!Object.hasOwn(decision,'value')`, `exec.parent === undefined`, `exec.name !== 'read'`; flattens `decision.content ?? result.content` via `flattenPlainText` (returns undefined if ANY block is non-text); measures `Buffer.byteLength(text,'utf8')` and returns unchanged if `<= maxInlineBytes`. When oversized it calls the shared `spillReplacement()` helper, which requires an owner session id (exec.agent?.session.header.id) and `ctx.get('spillStore')`, builds a `SaveTextSpill` with `suggestedName = `${toolName}.txt``, awaits `spillStore.saveText`, then reserves the notice's worst-case byte cost OUT of the budget and builds `preview + '

' + notice`; if the final replacement still exceeds the cap it returns undefined (keeps the inline content). On accept it returns `{ kind:'accept', content:[{type:'text',text:replacedText}], additionalContexts? }`.
invariants: Invariant: the policy NEVER emits a replacement larger than the cap — Reserve the notice's byte cost INSIDE maxInlineBytes so the replacement (preview + blank line + notice) never exceeds the documented cap (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:158-165 and 171-173).
A spill failure must NEVER turn a successful tool call into an `isError` or hide the inline result (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:33-35).
A bad config must fail the deployment, not the tool — maxInlineBytes is validated at load, not per call (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:109-111).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft (no session owner, no ctx.spillStore, saveText rejection, or no within-cap replacement each log a warning via ctx.logger.warn and return the ORIGINAL decision/content)
constants: maxInlineBytes: configured 50000 in the shipped base profile — packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:386; snapshot profiles use 800 — snapshots/session/parallel-tool-calls/cordis.snapshot.yml:52
omitted maxInlineBytes ⇒ plugin registers NOTHING (true no-op) — packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:108
load-time validation: must be a non-negative integer, `throw new Error('spill-policy: maxInlineBytes must be a non-negative integer (got ...)')` — packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:112-114
preview split: headBytes = Math.ceil(budget/2), tailBytes = Math.floor(budget/2) — packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:97-98

mechanisms.name: ptc-dispatch-log-durable-copy-bounding
mechanisms.what: Second arm of spill-policy: a prepended `tools/ptc-dispatch-log` waterfall listener (declared as a waterfall in packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:181, with @mode waterfall) that awaits `next()` and then applies the SAME `maxInlineBytes` cap to the session log's copy of an oversized run_code sub-call result, calling the shared `spillReplacement(..., 'dispatch')` with `dispatch.subCallId`. The program's returned value is untouched. This is the ONLY consumer path in-tree for the model-facing arm's helper on nested calls, because the post-execute arm skips `exec.parent !== undefined`. Unlike the post-execute arm, `read` sub-calls ARE spilled here (`flattenPlainText` is applied with no name filter). The registry invoker `ToolRuntime.shapeDispatchLog` contains a throwing listener by logging the original settled content.
invariants: The log copy is not model context, so the read → spill → read-again loop the post-execute arm avoids cannot happen here, and read is precisely the tool that produces huge logs (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:214-216).
Only the session log's copy shrinks to preview + locator, so replay and UIs read the full text through the spill artifact (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/index.ts:207-211).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft both ways: spillReplacement returning undefined keeps the original content, and a THROWING listener is contained by the registry invoker which logs a warning and returns the original settled content
constants: same cap as the model-facing arm (maxInlineBytes); no separate threshold

mechanisms.name: spill-notice-format-and-recognition
mechanisms.what:
Pure formatter/recognizer in spill-policy/src/notice.ts. `formatSpillNotice(omitted, ref)` composes `(${describeOmitted(omitted,'bytes')} Full formatted result stored at: ${ref.locator}. ${ref.retrievalHint})` from the constants OPEN='(', CLOSE=')', LOCATION=' Full formatted result stored at: ', GUIDANCE_SEPARATOR='. ', SEPARATOR='

'. `hasSpillNotice(text)` walks backwards through `

(` boundaries and validates the middle segment against `describeOmitted` for `none`/`unknown`/`exact` — the doc explicitly says this identifies the text convention, not authenticated provenance. Production caller: packages/client/ui-tool/src/client/tool/models/terminal-card-model.ts:5 imports `hasSpillNotice` and uses it at line 235 to detect a spilled terminal result for card rendering.
invariants: This identifies the text convention, not authenticated provenance of tool output (packages/spill/spill-policy/src/notice.ts:34-35).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft (pure, no I/O, no throws; `hasSpillNotice` returns false on any unrecognized shape)
constants: LOCATION = ' Full formatted result stored at: ' — packages/spill/spill-policy/src/notice.ts:7

mechanisms.name: bounded-output-retention-retainers
mechanisms.what: Dependency-light library (NOT a Cordis service/plugin: 'it takes no ctx, registers nothing, and emits no events'). Two stateful retainers: `ItemRetainer<T>` bounds an ordered stream of logical units with the single v1 strategy `{ kind:'head', maxItems }` — `push(item)` keeps while `items.length < maxItems` and otherwise counts an omission; `finish()` returns { items, truncated, seen, kept, omitted }. `TextRetainer` bounds a byte-oriented stream with `head`/`tail`/`headTail` byte budgets over one shared prefix/suffix accumulator; `push` fills the prefix up to `prefixCap`, rolls the suffix window to the last `suffixCap` bytes (trimming leading bytes of an oversized head chunk), and computes `kept`/`truncated` through the same `omittedAt(total) = total - min(total,prefixCap) - min(total-prefixLen,suffixCap)` used by `finish()`. `finish()` trims a trailing partial UTF-8 sequence off the prefix and leading continuation bytes off the suffix ONLY when a real omitted gap exists (otherwise it decodes the contiguous whole), and reports omission against the bytes ACTUALLY returned. `describeOmitted`/`formatRetentionNotice` are the standardized wording helpers. Production importers: spill-policy, tool-terminal/render.ts, tool-fs-search/search-core.ts, tool-jobs/index.ts, context/session-reference/projection.ts.
invariants: `truncated` means 'the retainer omitted otherwise-available content because of a budget' — NOT 'the upstream was incomplete'; permission failures, skipped binaries, provider partial failures, and unreadable candidates never fold into `truncated` (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:11-15).
Budget fields are non-negative integers: `assertBudget` throws `${name} must be a non-negative integer` otherwise (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:129-134).
The library never owns recovery words — only the tool does; `formatRetentionNotice` takes a caller-supplied recovery builder (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:428-431).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed on invalid budget (assertBudget throws from the constructor); the retainers themselves never throw on content and never reject
constants: no global numeric thresholds — every cap is caller-supplied; ItemRetentionStrategy.maxItems, TextRetentionStrategy maxBytes/headBytes/tailBytes are the only knobs (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:87-110)
UTF-8 trim walk bound: 'scan back at most 3 (max sequence is 4)' — packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:213-215
empty-string omission wording: 'Omitted N items.' / 'More items were omitted.' / '' for none — packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:412-421

mechanisms.name: repeat-tool-call-reminder-guard
mechanisms.what: Advisory per-agent consecutive-repeat detector registered by `apply` as a `tools/post-execute` waterfall listener plus an `agent/pre-step` reset hook. `observe(exec)` returns undefined when `!exec.agent` or the tool is untracked; otherwise it canonicalizes the arguments (deep key-sort via `sortJsonValue` then `JSON.stringify`), builds the chain key `JSON.stringify([exec.name, canonical])`, and advances a per-agent `WeakMap<Agent, Chain>` counter (same key ⇒ count+1, else 1). If the new count is in the threshold set it emits a `createUserMessage` with source { ...PLUGIN_SOURCE, form:'notice', summary: `${exec.name} × ${count}` } — GENTLE_REMINDER when `count === thresholds[0]`, otherwise detailedReminder with the tool name, count and head-truncated canonical arguments. The listener counts FIRST, then delegates via `await next()`, then folds the reminder onto whatever came back through `additionalContexts` (both decision variants including `block`). The `agent/pre-step` hook deletes the chain when any message has `source.kind === 'user'`. Tracking patterns are `*`-wildcards compiled to anchored RegExps; wildcard calls participate neither as count nor as reset. Wired in production: packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:419-423 with thresholds [3,5,8] and argumentsPreviewChars 500.
invariants: Observe-and-enrich, never veto: count first (state advances regardless of the downstream outcome), DELEGATE so a later listener can still block or replace, then fold the reminder onto whatever came back (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:209-212).

Misconfiguration fails loud: an empty `thresholds` list, a non-integer, a value below 2, or a duplicate throws at plugin load, never a silent fall-back (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:20-23).
The {kind:'plugin'} source label is load-bearing — an unlabeled context would render as a user prompt in derived history (packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:52-56).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed at plugin LOAD (validateThresholds and the argumentsPreviewChars check both throw), fail-open at runtime for the guarded call (it only prepends additionalContexts; it never blocks, rewrites, or vetoes, and always calls next())
constants: thresholds default [3, 5, 8] — packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:46; shipped profile repeats the same list — packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:422
argumentsPreviewChars default 500 and must be an integer >= 1 — packages/guard/repeat-tool-reminder/src/index.ts:49 and 169-171; shipped value 500 — packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:423

mechanisms.name: tool-call-timeout-policy-wrapper
mechanisms.what: Plugin `timeout-policy` (inject = ['tools']) registers a `tools/execute` wrapper named by the exported TOOL_TIMEOUT = 'TOOL_TIMEOUT'. Per call it reads `ctx.tools.get(exec.name, exec.agent)?.timeoutMs`; if undefined it delegates unchanged with `return next()`. Otherwise it creates `using d = deadline(exec.signal, timeoutMs, TOOL_TIMEOUT)`, swaps `exec.signal` to the derived deadline signal for dispatch (saving `upstream`), awaits `next()`, and — only when `timeoutOf(d.signal, TOOL_TIMEOUT) !== undefined` (i.e. THIS wrapper's own timer fired; a nested outer deadline reads as undefined) — replaces whatever the tool returned with `toolTimeoutResult(timeoutMs)`: `{ content:[{type:'text',text:'Error: tool call timed out after <N>ms'}], isError: true, error:{ message, info:{ name:'ToolTimeoutError', code: TOOL_TIMEOUT } } }`. The `finally` restores `exec.signal = upstream`. It has no config schema and no load-time validation. Wired in production: packages/bundle/base/cordis.patch.yml:377-378. Tools declare the budget through `ToolDefinition.timeoutMs` (packages/core/tools/src/index.ts:247, doc'd at 240-246 as never sent to the model and asserted cooperative).
invariants: Cooperative: a tool declares `timeoutMs` and promises to honor `exec.signal`; the wrapper arms that deadline and maps its own expiry to TOOL_TIMEOUT without racing or abandoning the tool promise (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:2-5).

Scoping timeoutOf to TOOL_TIMEOUT keeps a nested outer deadline from being misread as this plugin's own timeout — it reads as an ordinary upstream cancel (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:20-24).
post-execute listeners never see this plugin's (possibly already-aborted) timeout signal — the caller's own signal is restored in the finally (packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:62-64).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — the mapped expiry is fail-closed for the model (an isError=true TOOL_TIMEOUT result replaces the tool's own return once the wrapper's timer fired), but enforcement is purely cooperative: a tool that ignores exec.signal is awaited indefinitely, and any other error from the tool propagates unchanged
constants: TOOL_TIMEOUT = 'TOOL_TIMEOUT' (used as both the internal deadline classification code and the structured error code) — packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:25
model-facing message template `tool call timed out after ${timeoutMs}ms` — packages/guard/timeout-policy/src/index.ts:42

no numeric threshold in this package: the budget comes from each tool's own `timeoutMs` (e.g. tool-web attaches it at packages/web/tool-web/src/search.ts:362 and packages/web/tool-web/src/fetch.ts:498)

mechanisms.name: code-runtime-service-seam
mechanisms.what: Abstract Service Definition for `ctx.codeRuntime`: `abstract class CodeRuntime extends Service` with `super(ctx, 'codeRuntime')`, two informational abstract string properties `language` ('typescript' / 'python' are the well-known values) and `isolation` ('worker-thread' / 'process' / 'container'), and one abstract `run(request: CodeRunRequest): Promise<CodeRunResult>`. The module also owns the cross-backend portability vocabulary every backend must enforce identically: RESERVED_BINDING_GLOBALS = {console, __dsh_main__, __builtins__, __name__, __debug__}, RESERVED_ERROR_MEMBERS = {name, message, stack, args, with_traceback, add_note}, DUNDER_MEMBER = /^__.+__$/, and PORTABLE_RESERVED_WORDS (ECMAScript reserved words plus Python 3 keywords/soft keywords). The resolution contract is error-as-field: program/budget/abort/substrate failures resolve inside CodeRunResult while only Service Definition contract misuse rejects.
invariants: One shared reserved set — rather than each backend refusing only its own slots — keeps the portability promise real: a namespace list valid on one backend is valid on all (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/index.ts:27-31).
An error is a FIELD on a resolved result, never a rejection of run() — reporting a failed program is the caller's job, not an exception path (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/types.ts:110-113).

A request carries no optional tuning knobs for a hidden `??` to fill in — defaulting (time budgets, output caps) is the implementation's validated config (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/types.ts:67-72).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — resolved-result field for program/budget/abort/substrate failures (fail-soft across the seam); fail-closed (rejection) for Service Definition contract misuse
constants: PORTABLE_RESERVED_WORDS = ECMAScript reserved words + strict-mode names + Python 3 keywords/soft keywords incl. 'match','type','_' — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime/src/index.ts:75-86

mechanisms.name: worker-thread-code-runtime-isolation
mechanisms.what: `WorkerThreadCodeRuntime extends CodeRuntime` (language 'typescript', isolation 'worker-thread'), the shipped backend mounted by both bundles (packages/bundle/web-app/cordis.patch.yml:50-51 and packages/bundle/headless/cordis.patch.yml:20-21). `run()` rejects after disposal, validates bindings, returns an early `abort` result when the request signal is already aborted, then type-strips the program by wrapping it in `async function __dsh_program__() {\n` + program + `\n}` and calling `stripTypeScriptTypes`, slicing the body back out (a strip failure resolves as an `exception` result and NO worker spawns). `execute()` spawns `new Worker(WORKER_PATH, { workerData: bootData, env: {}, execArgv: [], resourceLimits: { maxOldGenerationSizeMb }, stdout: true, stderr: true })` and races four settle paths in `finish()` (idempotent, `settled` flag): done frame, `output-limit`, compute-budget ELU poll, wall timer, abort listener, worker `error`, worker `exit`. On settle it clears both timers, removes the abort listener, drops the run from `live`, waits one `setImmediate` for queued pipe bytes, then awaits `worker.terminate()` together with both pipe drains before resolving. Binding calls arrive as `call` messages, are de-duplicated by id (`answered` Set), resolved with `Object.hasOwn` own-property lookup only, and answered exactly once. Teardown marks `disposed`, settles every live run as `{kind:'abort', message:'runtime disposed'}` and awaits each `finished`.
invariants: This is containment, not a security boundary: model code has bash-equivalent trust despite an empty environment, a heap cap, measured event-loop busy-time and wall-time budgets, and termination that also stops synchronous loops (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:3-5).

Model code gets NO ambient environment — stronger than the scrubbed env the defensive-patterns rule requires for spawned commands (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:380-382).

Exactly one outcome wins. Every path cleans up, terminates, and awaits the worker; logs captured before timeout, abort, or failure remain in the result (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:420-422).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed for Service Definition misuse (run() after disposal and invalid binding namespaces THROW), fail-soft for everything a program can cause (strip failure, exception, invalid-output, output-limit, timeout, abort, worker-exit, worker error/exit all resolve as result.error); hostile port traffic is dropped silently (parseWorkerMessage returns undefined)
constants: maxWallMs default 600_000, and must be <= MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS (2_147_483_647) or load throws — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:241 and 267-269
MIN_OUTPUT_BYTES = 4 (empty logs array `[]` plus an empty JSON failure message) — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:66

OutputLedger starts at 2 bytes ('JSON serialization of the empty logs array: []') and charges 1 separator byte per extra entry — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:170 and 177
limit message template `outer output exceeded ${maxBytes} bytes` — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:200

mechanisms.name: worker-hostile-peer-frame-validation
mechanisms.what: `parseWorkerMessage(raw)` re-validates and REBUILDS every inbound port message field by field because the peer runs model code and can post anything; the compile-time WorkerToHost type means nothing here. It accepts only four discriminants: `call` requires typeof id === 'number' && typeof global === 'string' && typeof name === 'string'; `log` requires typeof text === 'string'; `output-limit` is swallowed with no fields; `done` requires either no `error` (optional `value`) or an error object whose kind is exactly one of 'exception' | 'invalid-output' | 'output-limit' with a string message. Everything else returns undefined and is dropped (a throw in the host's `message` listener would crash the host process).
invariants: a forged extra field never rides along; a non-number call id can never be echoed into a reply (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:136-139).

Parse before touching: the peer can post ANY shape, and a throw in this listener would crash the host process. Junk drops silently (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:509-512).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft (invalid traffic is dropped, returning undefined; the run continues and settles only via its real outcome paths)
constants: allowed done error kinds literal list: 'exception', 'invalid-output', 'output-limit' — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:160
protocol wire fields: WorkerBootData { code, namespaces[{global,names,errorClass?}], maxOutputBytes } — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/protocol.ts:11-22

mechanisms.name: outer-output-ledger-json-byte-accounting
mechanisms.what: `OutputLedger` (host) and `LogBuffer` (worker) are the two halves of one combined outer-output budget. The host ledger starts at 2 bytes (the `[]` of the logs array), charges each admitted log its exact JSON-string cost plus a separator byte (`jsonStringBytesUpTo`), and finalizes a completion value or failure diagnostic against the remaining budget via `jsonValueBytesUpTo`/`jsonStringBytesUpTo`. When the cap is crossed it builds `limit(logs)`: `outer output exceeded ${maxBytes} bytes`, computes the message's own byte cost (ASCII so length + 2 quotes), retains a fitting prefix of the final log with `truncateJsonStringBytes`, and returns `{ logs: retained, error: { kind: 'output-limit', message } }`. The worker-side `LogBuffer` mirrors the same accounting and, on exhaustion, emits the fitting prefix then reports the limit once via the `output-limit` frame. `jsonStringBytesUpTo` deliberately never materializes the escaped copy: it walks code points and returns undefined as soon as the cap is crossed. The measurement helpers capture intrinsics (Reflect.apply, Buffer.byteLength via Reflect.get, Object.create/defineProperty, String.prototype.slice/codePointAt/charCodeAt) so model-mutated prototypes cannot alter accounting.
invariants: Once exhausted it emits the fitting prefix and reports the limit once; the host turns that condition into an explicit `output-limit` run failure (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/bootstrap.ts:45-47).

Omission is reported against bytes ACTUALLY returned — an exact count derived from the budget alone would overstate the retained text (packages/util/output-retention/src/index.ts:372-375; the same principle drives the ledger's truncated-prefix accounting).
The fixed diagnostic is ASCII, so every character is one byte plus the quotes (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:201).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed for byte accounting: crossing the cap converts the run into an `output-limit` failure (never a silently truncated success)
constants: ledger initial bytes = 2 (empty logs array JSON) — host packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/index.ts:170; worker packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/bootstrap.ts:50
serialized char costs: lone surrogate 6, `\b\t\n\f\r` 2, other <0x20 6, `"`/`\` 2, astral pair 4 — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/output-json.ts:67-72
jsonValueBytesUpTo literal token costs: null 4, true 4, false 5, array/object 2 brackets — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/output-json.ts:115-128

mechanisms.name: worker-bootstrap-program-execution-and-binding-bridge
mechanisms.what: `runWorkerMain(port, data, streams)` builds a LogBuffer over `data.maxOutputBytes` that streams each admitted item to the host as a `log` frame and reports the limit once, patches `process.stdout`/`process.stderr` `write` slots through `captureStreamWrites`, wires host replies through `wireReplies`, mints one error constructor per declared namespace via `makeBindingErrorClasses`/`makeBindingErrorClass`, materializes null-prototype namespace objects with `makeNamespaces` (each declared name an own enumerable async function that snapshots arguments with `snapshotCodeJsonValue`, rejects on lossy args, posts a `call` with a worker-issued incrementing id and parks resolve/reject in a pending map), and creates a 5-method console shim using `util.inspect`. It then constructs an AsyncFunction from `(async () => {}).constructor` with the namespace globals, error-class parameters and `console` as parameters plus the literal body `'use strict';\n${data.code}`, awaits it, and posts exactly one terminal `done` message built by `prepareCompletion` (undefined → `{}`, lossless-JSON snapshot, else `invalid-output`, over-budget → `output-limit`) or by `prepareException`. `worker.ts` is the 14-line spawn-only entrypoint that throws if loaded outside a worker thread.
invariants: this null-prototype global per namespace — `__proto__`/`constructor`/`toString` are ordinary keys, never prototype collisions (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/bootstrap.ts:301-306).

Each reply settles its call at most once, and a reply for an unknown id (stray, or a duplicate answer to an id already settled) is ignored (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/bootstrap.ts:279-282).
Executable logic stays in bootstrap.ts for in-process coverage; real-worker tests cover this glue (packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/worker.ts:2-3).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft inside the worker: a binding failure rejects only that call (bindingFailure builds the namespace's declared error class, or a plain Error when none is declared); a thrown program error becomes the done frame's `error` field; lossy arguments reject before posting
constants: worker id counter starts at 1 (`const nextId = { value: 1 }`) — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/bootstrap.ts:385
array shape rule: ownKeys length must be exactly length + 1 (dense, no extra props) — packages/code-runtime/code-runtime-worker-thread/src/worker-json.ts:207

mechanisms.name: python-code-runtime
mechanisms.what: `PythonCodeRuntime extends CodeRuntime` (language 'python', isolation 'process'), the experimental/private CPython backend (package.json line 41 `"private": true`; only referenced by the snapshot profile snapshots/session/ptc-python-turn/cordis.yml:29-30, not by any shipped bundle). It throws at load on win32, validates all caps at load (positivity, integer cpuSeconds, safe-integer cpuSeconds+1 and addressSpaceMb*1MiB, non-empty NUL-free pythonBin, maxWallMs <= MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS, graceMs+CLOSE_REAP_MARGIN_MS <= MAX_TIMER_DELAY_MS, maxLogBytes/maxValueBytes integers and <= frameParseCapBytes - 64, maxLogBytes >= 64, and each output budget times a 12x worst-case Unicode expansion must fit addressSpaceMb minus a 64 MiB interpreter baseline), then resolves and probe-validates the interpreter once via `execFileSync(bin, ['-I','-c', ...])` with a 5 s SIGKILL timeout. Each `run()` synchronously materializes a per-run copy of `bootstrap.py`/`protocol.py` into `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(),'dsh-code-runtime-python-'))`, then `execute()` spawns `python3 -u -I <bootstrapPath>` with `env: { TMPDIR }` only, `detached: true` (own process group) and `stdio: ['pipe','pipe','pipe','pipe']` so fd 3 is the JSON-lines protocol channel (`PROTOCOL_FD = 3`), destroys the host stdin handle, and drives a per-line framed reader with a first-frame/whole-buffer parse cap. Settlement is a single idempotent `settle()` on the child's `close`; a timeout is classified ONLY on SIGXCPU (the kernel's RLIMIT_CPU meter). Kill escalation is SIGTERM → graceMs → SIGKILL on the process group, with a PID-reuse guard comparing `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22 start times, and a `closeDeadline` of graceMs + 2 s that force-settles a run whose `close` never fires because a setsid-escaped orphan holds the pipes.
invariants: This is containment, not a security boundary: model code has bash-equivalent trust, contained by a tempdir-only environment, RLIMIT_CPU + RLIMIT_AS, wall-clock timeout, and SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL on the process group (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:4-6).

The conversion is therefore wrapped, with a fixed literal as the fallback — the value already proved it cannot be rendered, so nothing derived from it is safe to try (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:409-418, on messageOf).

One copy per RUN, discarded at settlement — a rewrite then damages only the run that performed it, which is what fresh-subprocess-per-run already promises (packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:160-165).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — fail-closed at plugin LOAD (every config gate throws) and for seam misuse in run(); fail-soft for everything a program or the substrate can cause (staging failure, spawn failure, exception, invalid-output, output-limit, timeout, abort, worker-exit all resolve as result.error)
constants: defaults: cpuSeconds 60, maxWallMs 600_000, addressSpaceMb 512, maxLogBytes 65_536, maxValueBytes 32_768, graceMs 3_000, pythonBin 'python3' — packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:806-814
log ledger reserves 1 byte: `let logBudget = this.config.maxLogBytes - 1` — packages/experimental/code-runtime-python/src/index.ts:1265

mechanisms.name: e2b-shared-sandbox-owner
mechanisms.what: `E2BRuntime extends Service` registering `ctx.e2b`, which creates exactly ONE lazily-consumable E2B SDK handle at construction (`this.ready = this.open()`, with `void this.ready.catch(() => {})` so a failed eager connection stays observed) and deletes the sandbox at timeout or disposal. Config defaults are cwd '/home/user/workspace' and timeoutMs 300_000; `validate()` throws when the API key is empty (env E2B_API_KEY fallback), the cwd is not an absolute Linux path, or timeoutMs is not a positive finite number. `open()` resolves the control-plane URL via `e2bApiUrl()` (E2B_API_URL, then the loopback debug plane when E2B_DEBUG=true, then https://api.<E2B_DOMAIN|e2b.app>), asks `proxyRouteFor` for a proxy route, calls `Sandbox.create({ apiKey, timeoutMs, secure: true, lifecycle: { onTimeout: 'kill' }, proxy? })`, makes `cwd` and `runtimeRoot = <cwd>/.dsh-e2b`, verifies runtimeRoot is a real directory with no symlinkTarget, and chmods it 700 through `sandbox.commands.run` with `e2bControlEnvs()` (a fresh randomized HOME `/.dsh-e2b-control-<uuid>`). A setup failure kills the sandbox and rethrows. The disposer sets disposed, awaits readiness, and calls `sandbox.kill()` swallowing only SandboxNotFoundError. In-tree this package is referenced ONLY by its own test fixture (packages/e2b/e2b/tests/fixtures/composition/cordis.yml:5) — no shipped bundle mounts it.
invariants: Shared ownership of one E2B sandbox. Capability adapters await the same SDK handle, so filesystem and process operations inhabit one remote Linux world (packages/e2b/e2b/src/index.ts:2-3).
API key; omission reads E2B_API_KEY. It is never forwarded into the sandbox (packages/e2b/e2b/src/index.ts:46).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed (constructor validate() throws; getSandbox() throws 'E2B sandbox service is disposing' before and after awaiting readiness; a setup failure rolls back with sandbox.kill() and rethrows)
constants: sandbox lifecycle: `{ onTimeout: 'kill' }` and `secure: true` — packages/e2b/e2b/src/index.ts:163-164

mechanisms.name: fs-e2b-remote-filesystem-provider
mechanisms.what: `E2BFileSystem extends FileSystem` with `static inject = ['e2b']`, implementing the filesystem seam entirely inside the shared remote sandbox. `resolve` maps a display path to a canonical `targetKey` by running `set -o pipefail; realpath -mz -- <quoted path> | base64 -w0` over `sandbox.commands.run` and decoding with `decodeCanonicalPath` (strict base64 shape, NUL framing check, fatal UTF-8 decode, must be absolute). Reads are NUL-sampled over the first 8192 bytes and decoded with a fatal UTF-8 TextDecoder (`FS_NOT_TEXT` on either failure); `readBytes` enforces `maxBytes` twice — a stat preflight and a streamed bound that stops a post-stat grower without transferring past the first overflowing chunk; `readByteRange` skips to the offset and cancels the remote stream at the window end. Writes go through a per-target in-process promise chain (`withLock`, keyed by targetKey) and `writeAtomic`: a private staging directory `.dsh-<uuid>.tmp` chmod 700, the content written with `metadata: { 'dsh-version': <uuid> }`, `chmod <existing.mode & 0o777 | 0o600>`, then either `sandbox.files.rename` (replace) or a guarded create via `if ln -T -- <temp> <target>; then printf created; elif test -e <target> || test -L <target>; then printf exists; else exit 1; fi`. Versions are `e2b:sha256(JSON.stringify([metadata['dsh-version'], path, type, size, mode, modifiedTime, symlinkTarget]))`. Error mapping produces FsError codes FS_ABORTED / FS_NOT_FOUND / FS_PERMISSION_DENIED / FS_IO_ERROR (plus FS_NOT_TEXT, FS_TOO_LARGE, FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE, FS_NOT_OBSERVED, FS_STALE_VERSION, FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT, FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND, FS_NOT_DIRECTORY). In-tree this package is referenced ONLY by the e2b test fixture (packages/e2b/e2b/tests/fixtures/composition/cordis.yml:19) — no shipped bundle mounts it.
invariants: Paths, contents, and atomic staging files remain inside the shared remote sandbox (packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:2-3).
The stat preflight covers the at-rest case; this streamed bound stops a post-stat grower without transferring past the first overflowing chunk (packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:264-265).

The SDK streams only from the file's start: skip to `offset`, keep `length` bytes, and cancel the stream there, so no more than the window beyond the skipped prefix is ever transferred (packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:299-301).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed (every operation throws a coded FsError; a failed write removes its private staging directory and rethrows the mapped error)
constants: CRLF detection sample = first 4096 chars, CRLF wins only when crlf > lf — packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:43-46
staging directory name `.dsh-${randomUUID()}.tmp` with file `content` — packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:567-568
staging directory mode 0o700; new files get mode 0o600, existing files keep `existing.mode & 0o777` — packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:574 and 581-584
BASE64 shape regex for the canonical-path transport — packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:32
canonical-path command: `set -o pipefail; realpath -mz -- <arg> | base64 -w0` — packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:492
listDir uses `{ depth: 1 }` and sorts by name.localeCompare — packages/e2b/fs-e2b/src/index.ts:398 and 416

mechanisms.name: cordis-tool-extension
mechanisms.what: Model-facing Cordis runtime/package tool suite. `apply(ctx)` registers a `tool:cordis` systemPrompt section (order from `ctx.systemPrompt.getSectionOrder('TOOL_CORDIS')`), registers each `hostInspectProviders(ctx)` provider through `ctx.effect(() => ctx.cordisInspect.register(provider), ...)`, and registers seven tools via `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))`: cordis_inspect_list, cordis_inspect_query (delegates to `ctx.cordisInspect.query(platform, provider, method, input, requireAgent(exec), exec.signal)`), cordis_inspect_self (three detail levels; rejects `packageId` without `pluginId`), cordis_define (kind 'new' with a 3–6 lowercase-letter idPrefix, or kind 'existing' with an exact pluginId; validates and records source but does NOT run), cordis_run (mode 'run'|'update' through `ctx.dynamicCordisRunner.run`, then reports host/client waiting status via `missingServices`/`providedServices`), cordis_stop, and cordis_undefine. A final `agent/pre-step` waterfall listener scans USER messages for `@<id>` references with `/(?:^|\s)@([a-z]{3,6}-\d+)(?=\s|$)/g` and appends one plugin-sourced context message per referenced plugin (identity, default base package, version pointers, runtime status — not source). `inject = ['tools','systemPrompt','dynamicCordisRunner','cordisInspect']`. Wired in production: packages/preset/agent-presets/presets/cordis/agent.cordis.yml:247 and apps/cli/config/examples/cordis/cordis.yml:19.
invariants: cordis_define only defines and presents code; it does not run it (packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/prompt.ts:17).

Never silently create another Plugin for @pluginId. If the reference is unavailable because it was removed, belongs to another Session, or was lost on process restart, tell the user directly (packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/prompt.ts:54).
A single check mark authorizes only the current Package; double check marks authorize future versions of the same Plugin (packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/prompt.ts:45).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed (a tool call without an Agent-backed session throws 'Cordis dynamic tools require an Agent-backed session'; bad arguments, unknown inspect methods and failed runner receipts throw; `requireJsonObject`/`requireJsonString` throw on malformed render input)
constants: catalogProvider exact-input shape `{ type:'object', properties:{[field]:{type:'string'}}, additionalProperties:false }` — packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/providers.ts:94
FiberState mirror values PENDING 0 / LOADING 1 / ACTIVE 2 / FAILED 3 / DISPOSED 4 / UNLOADING 5 — packages/extensions/tool-cordis/src/fiber-state.ts:11-18

mechanisms.name: agent-loop-parallel-tool-call-execution
mechanisms.what: `executeToolCalls(ctx, turn, step, toolCalls, signal, acceptContext)` (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:60) is the scheduler for one assistant step's tool calls. It plans every call once (`PlannedCall[]`, arguments parsed by `parseArguments`, distinct exec objects because tools/execute wrappers may replace exec.signal) and then loops: it reads `ctx.tools.executionMode(planned[next]).kind` for the FIRST unstarted call; `'parallel'` takes `planned.slice(next)` as the group, any other mode takes `[first]` as a one-call exclusive barrier group; `runGroup` returns `{consumed, aborted, concluded}` and `next += outcome.consumed`. Inside `runGroup`: `maxParallelToolCalls` comes from `ctx.agentLoop.config` (DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS = 10, packages/core/agent-loop/src/constants.ts:6); `fillPool()` starts calls while `!aborted && nextToStart < group.length && inFlight.size < maxParallelToolCalls`; a later call that is no longer parallel BREAKS the pool (`nextToStart > 0 && mode === 'parallel' && ctx.tools.executionMode(nextCall.exec).kind !== 'parallel'`), so it stays for the caller's next barrier. Each start appends its `tool/call` event first, then awaits `ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare(exec)` which resolves to 'dispatch' | 'post-result' | 'final-result'; only 'dispatch' overlaps (its promise is registered in `inFlight`). Concurrency is driven by `await Promise.race(inFlight.values())` in the drain loop, then `commitReady()`, then `fillPool()` again. COMMIT ORDERING: `commitReady()` advances a `committed` cursor only across CONTIGUOUS model-order slots — it stops at the first `slots[committed] === undefined` — for each ready slot it awaits `finalize(exec, result)` when `needsPost` else calls `finish(exec, result)`, then `appendToolResult(session, turn, step, call.block, result, callSeqs[committed])` and forwards every `result.additionalContexts` to `acceptContext`. So dispatch overlaps but policy/`tools/post-execute` finalization, result appends and result-context acceptance happen strictly in model order. Abort: `aborted` is re-read after every await; the group stops starting, drains and COMMITS already-started calls, then appends synthetic `tool/result` events (isError true, 'tool call aborted before dispatch', code TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH) for every remaining model call in order via `appendSkippedToolCall`, and `executeToolCalls` does the same for calls beyond the consumed prefix before returning. Scheduler failure: the first `prepare`/`dispatch` rejection is stored in `schedulerFailure`, rethrown at each step boundary, `inFlight` is drained with `Promise.allSettled`, and the error is thrown WITHOUT fabricating tool results. `appendToolResult` records the result citing the call's seq through `{ surfaceOp: 'append', sourceEventSeqs: [callSeq] }`.
invariants: Dispatch may overlap, while policy, results, and result context remain model-ordered (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:4-5).
`committed` advances only across contiguous model-order slots (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:146).

Commit before classifying again so registry changes affect unstarted calls (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:86); Re-read later modes after ordered commits so registry changes can create a barrier (packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:201).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — abort is fail-soft with synthetic ordered error results (replay stays valid, started-call context is still accepted); an internal scheduler failure is fail-closed: replenishment stops, started dispatches drain, and the first error is rethrown to the turn boundary without fabricating tool results
constants: adapter validation: `maxParallelToolCalls must be a positive integer` when not an integer or < 1 — packages/core/agent-loop/src/index.ts:191-193

abort result literal: content 'Error: tool call aborted before dispatch', isError true, error.info { name:'AbortError', code: TOOL_ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH } — packages/core/agent-loop/src/tool-calls.ts:253-258
